import { Aside, CardGrid, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Everything your app can ask the node to do at runtime goes through a host
function. The SDK wraps each one as a plain Rust function under
`calimero_sdk::env`, defined in `crates/sdk/src/env.rs`. On `wasm32` these call
into the host across the WASM boundary; off-`wasm32` (the in-process test
harness) they route to a native mock.

This page is the app-author reference: *what can my app call, and what does it
do*. For the wire-level ABI (registers, buffer descriptors, return-code
conventions) see [`execution`](/protocol/execution/) and the runtime's
`crates/runtime/HOST_FUNCTIONS.md`.

<Aside type="note">
  Bring the functions into scope with `use calimero_sdk::env;` and call them as
  `env::device_id()`, `env::log(..)`, and so on. Most apps reach for only a
  handful — identity, logging, events, and time. State lives in CRDT
  collections, not in raw `env::storage_*` calls; see
  [`collections`](/build/collections/).
</Aside>

## Context & identity

Who is running, in which context, and on whose behalf.

| Function | What it does | Gotcha |
|----------|--------------|--------|
| `env::context_id() -> [u8; 32]` | The 32-byte ID of the context this execution runs in. | Same for every member of the context. Not an identity — don't use it to authorize a caller. |
| `env::account_id() -> [u8; 32]` | The 32-byte account this call is authorized as — a **person**, not a machine. | The actor for per-user logic: `Map<account_id, Vote>` is one vote per person, whichever passkey (device) they signed in with. For a run the node fires itself (a handler, a timer, an xcall) it is the app's own id; see [Who a run acts as](/protocol/authorship/). |
| `env::device_id() -> [u8; 32]` | The executor's 32 bytes: on a cluster, the caller's account, as `account_id()` and `executor_id()` are. | There are no per-device keys: two passkeys of one person are the same executor. A CRDT's own mechanics (an LWW tiebreak, a counter slot, an HLC seed) key off it. |
| `env::xcall_origin() -> Option<[u8; 32]>` | The context that dispatched the current cross-context call, or `None` for a client's call. | Set by the node from the calling context — it cannot be forged. Return-`None` lets a method reject direct calls and require xcall-only invocation. |
| `env::input() -> Option<Vec<u8>>` | The raw, undecoded input bytes for this call (typically JSON-encoded arguments). | `#[app::logic]` already decodes method arguments for you. You only need `input()` for custom entry points or raw payloads. |

## Output

How a method's return value (or error) leaves the WASM module.

| Function | What it does | Gotcha |
|----------|--------------|--------|
| `env::value_return(result: &Result<T, E>)` | Sets the final return value — the `Ok` or `Err` variant the caller receives. | **Macro-driven.** You don't call this; the `#[app::logic]` codegen serializes your method's return value to JSON and calls it. |
| `env::commit(root_hash: &[u8; 32], artifact: &[u8])` | Commits the execution's state root and the commit artifact the node turns into the run's diff. | **Macro-driven.** Emitted by the generated method wrapper. Called exactly once per mutating call; never call it yourself. |

<Aside type="note">
  `value_return` and `commit` are listed here so the model is complete, but
  they're part of the generated method boundary. Returning a value (or an
  `Err`) from your method is how you drive them — see
  [`error-handling`](/build/error-handling/).
</Aside>

## Logging

| Function | What it does | Gotcha |
|----------|--------------|--------|
| `env::log(message: &str)` | Appends a UTF-8 line to the execution log, surfaced in the node logs and the execution outcome. | Logs are bounded (`max_logs`, `max_log_size`). Prefer the `app::log!("..", x)` macro for formatting. Logging is a side effect, not state — it is not replicated. |

### `tracing` integration

With the optional `tracing` cargo feature enabled, the SDK installs a
host-backed `tracing` subscriber at method entry (`env::init_logging()`, wired
into every generated export). From then on, `tracing::info!`/`debug!`/… calls —
**from your app and from any crate it depends on** — are formatted and forwarded
to the same host log as `env::log`, with no per-app setup.

<Aside type="caution" title="Default level is WARN, and DEBUG leaks storage internals">
  The default forwarded level is **`WARN`**, not `INFO` — so `info!`/`debug!`
  lines are silently dropped out of the box. (The default is deliberately
  conservative: dependencies like `calimero_storage` log routine operations at
  `INFO`, which would otherwise flood every execution's log buffer.) Retune it at
  runtime with `env::set_log_level(LevelFilter::..)`; the change takes effect
  immediately, even for the already-installed subscriber.

  At `DEBUG` (and below), `tracing` from *every* crate compiled into the guest is
  forwarded — including `calimero_storage` internals (keys, values, merge
  detail). Those lines land in the persisted execution `Outcome`, so treat
  `DEBUG` as a transient debugging aid, not something to leave on where the
  `Outcome` is stored or exposed.
</Aside>

## Events

Structured notifications for clients, delivered on the app's event stream
(`GET /apps/{app}/events`, [Reads](/protocol/reads/#events)). An event type implements `AppEvent`; in practice you derive it with
`#[app::event]`.

| Function | What it does | Gotcha |
|----------|--------------|--------|
| `env::emit(event: &T)` | Emits an event with a `kind` and serialized `data`. | Bounded by `max_events` / `max_event_data_size`. Events are observational: they don't mutate state. They are part of the run's outcome, committed with its entry and streamed to clients. |
| `env::emit_with_handler(event: &T, handler: &str)` | Emits an event and names a handler method to run after it is processed. | Handlers may run **in parallel** and out of order — they must be commutative, idempotent, and side-effect-free (CRDT-only). See the SDK `event` module notes. |

<Aside type="tip">
  Use `app::emit!(MyEvent { .. })` rather than calling `env::emit` directly —
  the macro wires up `kind`/`data` for you. See
  [`sdk-macros`](/build/sdk-macros/).
</Aside>

## Crypto

| Function | What it does | Gotcha |
|----------|--------------|--------|
| `env::ed25519_verify(signature: &[u8; 64], public_key: &[u8; 32], message: &[u8]) -> bool` | Verifies an Ed25519 signature over `message` for `public_key`. | Returns `true`/`false`; it does not bail on an invalid signature — check the bool. Has no native mock: it panics under `TestHost`. |

### Example: accepting an off-chain-signed voucher

A voucher is signed by a trusted issuer *off* the network; the app accepts it
only if the signature checks out, then records the redemption and emits an event
so off-chain consumers can react. This pairs `env::ed25519_verify` (trust the
payload) with `app::emit!`/`env::emit` (announce the outcome).

```rust
use calimero_sdk::{app, env};
use calimero_storage::collections::UnorderedSet;

#[app::state(emits = for<'a> Event<'a>)]
pub struct Shop {
    issuer_pk: [u8; 32],           // the trusted issuer's public key
    redeemed: UnorderedSet<String>, // codes already used (anti-replay)
}

#[app::event]
pub enum Event<'a> {
    VoucherRedeemed { code: &'a str, amount: u64 },
}

#[app::logic]
impl Shop {
    pub fn redeem(
        &mut self,
        code: String,
        amount: u64,
        signature: [u8; 64],
    ) -> app::Result<()> {
        // The issuer signs the exact bytes `"<code>:<amount>"` off-chain.
        // Reconstruct them identically and verify before trusting anything.
        let message = format!("{code}:{amount}");
        if !env::ed25519_verify(&signature, &self.issuer_pk, message.as_bytes()) {
            app::bail!("invalid voucher signature");
        }
        // `ed25519_verify` returns a bool — a bad signature does not bail on
        // its own, so the guard above is load-bearing.
        if !self.redeemed.insert(code.clone())? {
            app::bail!("voucher already redeemed");
        }
        app::emit!(Event::VoucherRedeemed { code: &code, amount });
        Ok(())
    }
}
```

`UnorderedSet::insert` returns `false` when the value was already present, which
doubles as the anti-replay check. The signed `message` must be byte-identical to
what the issuer signed — a different separator or number format fails
verification.

## Time & randomness

<Aside type="note">
  Only the app's leader runs a call, and the other replicas apply the diff it
  wrote, so a value read from `time_now` or `random_bytes` is read once and
  every replica holds the same result ([Execution](/protocol/execution/)).
  A run that a leader change makes run again reads them again.
</Aside>

| Function | What it does | Gotcha |
|----------|--------------|--------|
| `env::time_now() -> u64` | The current Unix timestamp in **nanoseconds**. | The leader's wall clock. |
| `env::random_bytes(buf: &mut [u8])` | Fills `buf` with random bytes from the host. | The leader's randomness. Under the test harness it is a deterministic, **non-cryptographic** PRNG: don't rely on it for security in tests. |
| `env::tee_random_bytes(buf: &mut [u8])` | Fills `buf` with randomness drawn inside an attested TEE. | Traps outside a TEE-triggered run (an `#[app::tee]` method the TEE scheduler fired). See [TEE authorship](/protocol/tee-authorship/). |
| `env::tee_origin() -> bool` | Whether this run was fired by the TEE scheduler as the TEE authority. | Set by the node, never by a caller. `#[app::tee]` checks it for you. |
| `env::seal_to(key: &[u8; 32], plaintext: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>>` | Seals `plaintext` so that only a run whose executor is `key` can open it, and only in the context it was sealed in. | Proves confidentiality, never authorship: anyone who knows a key can seal to it. Keep what the TEE seals in `TeeOnly` state. `None` if `key` is not a usable Ed25519 point. |
| `env::open_sealed(sealed: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>>` | Opens an envelope sealed to this run's executor key, or, in a TEE-triggered run, to the app's TEE key. | `None` for an envelope sealed to another key or in another context. Prefer `Sealed<T>` / `TeeSecret<T>` from `calimero-storage`. |
| `env::tee_sealing_key() -> Option<[u8; 32]>` | The app's TEE key, which a value only the TEE may read is sealed to. The node derives it per app: the cluster is every app's TEE. | Every run: the key is public. |
| `env::tee_authority_keys() -> Vec<[u8; 32]>` | The keys a value only the TEE may read is sealed to: the app's TEE key. | TEE-triggered runs only. `TeeSecret<T>` seals to these on every write. |
| `env::account_device_keys(account: &[u8; 32]) -> Vec<[u8; 32]>` | The key standing for `account` in this app, which the node derives per app and account: what a value only that member may read is sealed to, so their own runs open it. Empty for an account that does not reach the app. | TEE-triggered runs only. `Sealed::to_account` seals to these. |

## Shared writer sets

A `SharedStorage` cell keeps its writer set beside the cell, in the host's key space, not in the cell. Rotating it is a request your run records; the node checks it after the run and writes the new set in the same entry ([Execution](/protocol/execution/#what-the-node-checks-after-the-run)). You rarely call these directly: `SharedStorage` and the collections built on it do.

| Function | What it does | Gotcha |
|----------|--------------|--------|
| `env::shared_writers(cell: &[u8; 32]) -> Option<Option<Vec<u8>>>` | The borsh-encoded writers of `cell` in the state this run reads. `None` if they cannot be resolved, `Some(None)` if no rotation took effect (the set stored with the cell stands), `Some(Some(bytes))` for a rotated set. | Fail closed on `None`. Under `TestHost` every cell is at genesis. |
| `env::shared_writers_rotate(rotation: &[u8])` | Records a borsh-encoded rotation request on the run's outcome. | Nothing is stored by the run: the node writes the new set if the rotation holds. The run itself reads the new set back at once. At most 64 requests per run, 256 writers per set. |

## Cross-context calls

| Function | What it does | Gotcha |
|----------|--------------|--------|
| `env::xcall(context_id: &[u8; 32], function: &str, params: &[u8])` | Queues a call to `function` in another context of the same organization, run by that context's leader **after** this entry commits. | Fire-and-queue: it returns no value to the caller and is not executed inline. The target method must be `#[app::xcall]`. Has no native mock (panics under `TestHost`). Prefer the typed `#[app::xcall]` surface. |

See [`xcall`](/protocol/xcall/) for the dispatch and authorization model, and
[`advanced-sdk`](/build/advanced-sdk/) for the typed wrapper.

## Blobs

Streaming large binary objects. You write through a handle, finalize to get a
content-addressed 32-byte ID, then the context's app can open that ID for reading.
A blob is the app's when its state marks it (the app wrote it, or a client
uploaded it to the app); a node that misses the bytes fetches them from
another node of the cluster.

| Function | What it does | Gotcha |
|----------|--------------|--------|
| `env::blob_create() -> u64` | Opens a new write handle; returns a file descriptor. | The descriptor is only valid for this execution. |
| `env::blob_write(fd: u64, data: &[u8]) -> u64` | Appends `data` to the write handle; returns bytes written. | Stream in chunks for large payloads rather than one huge buffer. |
| `env::blob_close(fd: u64) -> [u8; 32]` | Finalizes a write handle and returns the blob's 32-byte ID (or, for a read handle, returns its ID and cleans up). | Panics if finalization fails. The ID is content-addressed — identical bytes yield the same ID. |
| `env::blob_open(blob_id: &[u8; 32]) -> u64` | Opens an existing blob for reading; returns a file descriptor. | The blob must be the app's (its state marks it). Any other blob traps with `BlobNotHeldForContext`. |
| `env::blob_open_in_context(blob_id: &[u8; 32], context_id: &[u8; 32]) -> u64` | Opens one of the app's blobs, as `blob_open` does. | `context_id` must be `env::context_id()`; any other traps with `BlobContextMismatch`. Returns `0` if the blob is not the app's. |
| `env::blob_read(fd: u64, buffer: &mut [u8]) -> u64` | Reads into `buffer`; returns bytes read. | Returns `0` at end of blob — loop until it does. |
| `env::blob_announce_to_context(blob_id: &[u8; 32], target_context_id: &[u8; 32]) -> bool` | Whether the blob is the app's. A cluster has nothing to announce: every node holds or fetches the app's blobs. | A context may only name **itself**: the SDK returns `false` for any other `target_context_id`, and the host traps with `BlobContextMismatch`. |

See [Blobs](/protocol/blobs/) for how the cluster stores them.

## Search

Full-text search over the app's indexes on the node that runs the view; most apps use the
typed `calimero_sdk::search` API on top of it. See
[Search your app's data](/build/guides/search/).

| Function | What it does | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `env::search(request: &SearchRequest) -> Result<SearchResponse, String>` | Queries this context's index `request.index`; hits are entity ids, best first. | Views only: a mutating method that calls it traps. Charged `8,000 + 25·matched + 18,500·hits + 125·response bytes` gas; at most 32 calls per execution. `Err` is the node's refusal (unknown field, substring under 3 characters). |

## Private storage

The caller's own key/value space in the app's state: replicated with it and
sealed on disk like the rest, but handed only to runs whose caller is that
account. App code cannot address another account's space
([Execution](/protocol/execution/#three-storage-spaces-in-one-state)).

| Function | What it does | Gotcha |
|----------|--------------|--------|
| `env::private_storage_read(key: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>>` | Reads a value from the caller's space. | `None` means "no such key", or a run with no caller account (a public call). |
| `env::private_storage_write(key: &[u8], value: &[u8]) -> bool` | Writes a value to the caller's space. | Returns `true` on success, `false` if the run has no private space. This bool is success/failure, unlike `storage_write`, whose bool means "a previous value was evicted". |
| `env::private_storage_remove(key: &[u8]) -> bool` | Removes a value from the caller's space. | `true` if the key existed and was removed, `false` if absent or unavailable. |

See [Access-controlled storage](/build/permissioned-storage/#the-callers-private-state)
for `#[app::private]`, the typed layer on top.

## JS runtime collection bridge

The Rust SDK calls the storage layer directly, so its CRDT writes flow into the
Merkle DAG and the outcome artifact automatically. The QuickJS runtime cannot —
JavaScript has no access to the Rust storage interface. Instead it funnels its
state back through a dedicated set of host functions that reproduce, host-side,
what the Rust SDK does in-process. These are defined in
`crates/runtime/src/logic/host_functions/system.rs` and `js_collections.rs`.

The root-state bridge keeps the storage tree and the outcome artifact in step:

| Host function | Role |
|---------------|------|
| `persist_root_state(doc_ptr, created_at, updated_at)` | Saves the serialized root document through the storage interface (recomputing parent hashes and emitting a CRDT action) rather than writing raw bytes. Its writes are held to the `storage_write` caps and per-execution write budget. |
| `read_root_state(register_id) -> i32` | Loads the persisted root document into a register; returns `1` if it exists, `0` if not. |
| `apply_storage_delta(delta_ptr)` | Applies a Borsh-encoded `StorageDelta`, updating CRDT entities and the root atomically, then refreshes the root hash. Its writes are held to the `storage_write` caps and per-execution write budget. |
| `flush_delta() -> i32` | Emits the CRDT actions recorded since the last flush into the run's artifact; returns `1` if there were any, `0` if there was nothing to commit. |

<Aside type="caution" title="The collection bridge uses a different error ABI">
  The `js_crdt_*` and `js_user_storage_*` collection host functions (e.g.
  `js_crdt_map_insert`, `js_user_storage_insert`) do **not** trap on error. They
  return `i32` where:

  - `1` — success *with* a result (e.g. a previous value was written into the
    destination register),
  - `0` — success with *no* result (not found / no previous value),
  - `-1` — **error**, with the error message written as UTF-8 into the
    destination register (see `write_error_message` in `js_collections.rs`).

  So a caller that checks `result == 1` to mean "ok" silently swallows both the
  legitimate `0` case **and** the `-1` error case — the error string sits unread
  in the register and execution continues as if nothing failed. The correct
  pattern is to treat `-1` as the error branch (read the message out of the
  register) and `0`/`1` as the two success shapes.
  A write over the storage caps or past the execution's write budget is the
  exception: it traps, like `storage_write`.
</Aside>

<Aside type="caution">
  The cross-context, blob and signature helpers have no in-process mock and
  panic under `TestHost`, and `http_request` answers `Err` there: test the
  logic around them by passing their results in.
</Aside>
